record.paper_title: Fluctuation Limit of Branching Processes with Immigration and Estimation of the Means
record.context_brief: Estimator normalization in degenerate variance regime
record.original_question: Consider a triangular sequence of Galton-Watson branching processes with immigration X_k^(n), started from X_0^(n)=0, where m_n = 1 + alpha/n + o(1/n), sigma_n^2 = beta/n + o(1/n), lambda_n tends to lambda > 0, and b_n^2 tends to b^2. Let the conditional least-squares estimator of m_n be formed from the regression X_k^(n)=m_n X_{k-1}^(n)+lambda_n+M_k^(n) when lambda_n is known, and let the joint conditional least-squares estimators estimate (m_n, lambda_n) when both means are unknown. In the fully degenerate variance regime beta=0 and b^2=0, the normal limits obtained with the norming factors n^{3/2} for the m_n estimators and n^{1/2} for the lambda_n estimator collapse to point masses. What replacement normalization and limiting distribution, if any, describe these least-squares estimators in that degenerate regime?

evidence.quote: Thus, in this case, we find that n3/2(mn − mn) p−→ 0, n3/2(mn − mn) p−→ 0, and n1/2(λn − λn) p −→ 0 as n → ∞, which means that the norming factors n3/2 and n1/2 are not appropriate.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each integer n ≥ 1, let (X_k^{(n)})_{k ≥ 0} be a Galton–Watson branching process with immigration, defined on a common probability space, with X_0^{(n)} = 0 and the recursion

  X_k^{(n)} = sum_{j=1}^{X_{k-1}^{(n)}} ξ_{k,j}^{(n)} + ε_k^{(n)},  k = 1, 2, …,

where, for each n, {ξ_{k,j}^{(n)} : k, j ≥ 1} are i.i.d. nonnegative integer-valued offspring random variables with mean m_n = E ξ_{1,1}^{(n)} and variance σ_n^2 = Var ξ_{1,1}^{(n)}, and {ε_k^{(n)} : k ≥ 1} are i.i.d. nonnegative integer-valued immigration random variables, independent of the offspring variables, with mean λ_n = E ε_1^{(n)} and variance b_n^2 = Var ε_1^{(n)}. Assume the nearly critical regime

  m_n = 1 + α/n + o(1/n),  σ_n^2 = β/n + o(1/n),  λ_n → λ > 0,  b_n^2 → b^2,

as n → ∞, with α ∈ ℝ and β, b^2 ≥ 0.

Writing the regression form X_k^{(n)} = m_n X_{k-1}^{(n)} + λ_n + M_k^{(n)} with martingale differences M_k^{(n)}, define for a sample of size n:
 • the conditional least-squares estimator m̃_n of m_n when λ_n is known,
 • the joint conditional least-squares estimators (m̂_n, λ̂_n) of (m_n, λ_n) when both means are unknown.

In the nondegenerate case (β > 0 or b^2 > 0) it is known that n^{3/2}(m̃_n − m_n), n^{3/2}(m̂_n − m_n), and n^{1/2}(λ̂_n − λ_n) converge in distribution to nondegenerate normal laws. In the fully degenerate variance regime β = 0 and b^2 = 0, however, these normalized quantities converge in probability to 0, so the factors n^{3/2} and n^{1/2} are not the correct rates.

Determine the appropriate norming sequences a_n, a'_n, c_n and identify the (necessarily nondegenerate) limiting distributions, if they exist, of

  a_n (m̃_n − m_n),  a'_n (m̂_n − m_n),  c_n (λ̂_n − λ_n),

as n → ∞ under the degenerate regime β = 0, b^2 = 0.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search located related literature on conditional least-squares estimation in (nearly) critical branching processes with immigration and on variance estimation under non-homogeneous immigration, but no source was found that explicitly identifies the correct normalization and limiting distribution for the offspring-mean and immigration-mean CLS estimators in the fully degenerate variance regime β = 0, b² = 0. The status of this specific question could not be conclusively verified.

status_evidence.title: Fluctuation limit of branching processes with immigration and estimation of the means
status_evidence.snippet: Treats nearly critical branching processes with immigration and CLS estimation of the means with norming n^{3/2} and n^{1/2}.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the nondegenerate-regime limits whose collapse motivates the open question.

status_evidence.title: Variance estimators in critical branching processes with non-homogeneous immigration
status_evidence.snippet: Studies CLS variance estimators in critical branching processes with non-homogeneous immigration.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on estimators in critical regimes; does not resolve the degenerate β=0, b^2=0 normalization question.

status_evidence.title: Critical branching processes with immigration
status_evidence.snippet: Survey/extension of fluctuation limits for critical branching processes with immigration.
status_evidence.claim: Related survey; does not provide the alternative norming in the fully degenerate regime.
